ios.desc:
Play with numbers in eight languages and make verb conjugation fun – Lexie is a tamagotchi-style counting game that turns language practice into a cosy pocket companion.

Forget long lessons. Lexie focuses on the tricky bits most apps rush through: numbers you can actually say out loud and verb conjugation that sticks. Quick quiz rounds, voice practice and listening games – all wrapped in a cute virtual pet you'll want to keep happy.


  MEET YOUR LANGUAGE PET
  Lexie is a tiny blob who lives in your phone:
  • Keep Lexie happy by practising daily
  • Earn coins and hearts as you play
  • Level up and unlock new looks
  • A gentle, cosy companion – not a stress machine

  WHO LEXIE IS FOR
  • Kids learning a language at school
  • Parents wanting educational screen time that's actually fun
  • Teens drilling for language tests and exams
  • Adults brushing up numbers for travel or work
  • Anyone who loves tamagotchi games and wants their playtime to count


  NUMBERS & VERBS, NOT EVERYTHING
  Lexie is a focused drill game, not a full course:
  • French numbers – including the hard 70s, 80s and 90s
  • Counting practice in seven more languages
  • Core verb conjugation and tense patterns
  • Spell, pronounce and say numbers with confidence

  Perfect as a warm-up before class, quick review before a test, or daily brain snack.

  THREE WAYS TO PLAY

  QUIZ MODE
  Tap your way through fast multiple-choice rounds:
  • Match numbers to their written word form
  • Pick the correct conjugation for every person
  • Great for quiet counting practice anywhere

  VOICE MODE
  Speak your answer and let Lexie listen:
  • Say numbers and verbs out loud
  • Get instant feedback on pronunciation
  • Build real speaking confidence without a teacher

  LISTEN MODE
  Press play and absorb:
  • Hear numbers read aloud in the language you're learning
  • Passive practice while you relax
  • Develop a natural feel for rhythm and sound

  SET YOUR OWN LEVEL
  Choose Easy, Medium or Hard and Lexie stays there:
  • First rounds start small, then grow with you
  • Move up when the numbers stop feeling like work
  • Or leave it on Auto, where difficulty follows how well you've been answering

  SHARPEN WHAT YOU KNOW
  Already speak a little? Lexie helps you:
  • Stop hesitating when saying numbers
  • Make verb tense feel automatic
  • Refresh skills after a break from class
  • Turn spare minutes into real practice

  STARTING FROM SCRATCH?
  Beginners welcome too:

quotes.text:
Hey HN! Halfway through moving to Canada and whilst my conversational French gets me by, I'm absolutely rubbish when someone rattles off phone numbers at full speed (quatre-vingt-dix-neuf anyone?).

So I built a virtual pet that thrives on correctly answered number challenges. 20-second drills throughout the day: get them right and Lexie grows, get them wrong and it gets a bit sad (but never dies, this isn't the 90s).

Speak, type, or tap your answers. Would love any feedback/bugreports.

Or just rant about how the Belgians sensibly say "nonante-neuf" whilst we're stuck with "four-twenties-nineteen".
